headline: South Asia: Elon Musk calls on Zelensky to 'go' as Ukraine leader
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Elon Musk calls on Zelensky to 'go' as Ukraine leader.
- Korean Peninsula: How North Korean missiles found their way into Houthi hands.
- Western Russia: Ukrainian Navy strikes six Russian Su-34M bombers with Neptune missile.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Disrupt, Strike, Assault and Endure: The 4 pillars of the US Army’s new warfare guidance.
- Military Times, 15 hours ago: Disrupt, Strike, Assault and Endure: The 4 pillars of the US Army’s new warfare guidance.
“How The Army Fights” is a new 46-page U.S. Army-issued guide on how the service should fight — and survive — on the modern battlefield.
- Military Times, 19 hours ago: US Army taps 9 companies to build next-gen command and control software.
The service announced contract awards worth $93.6 million across nine companies building applications for its Next Generation Command and Control software.
- Military Times, 18 hours ago: ‘You’re a coward’: Protesters heckle Hegseth during AUSA panel.
Protesters derailed a Washington, D.C., panel featuring Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth on Wednesday, calling him a “war criminal” and “Nazi.”
The Caribbean - bottom line: Reckoning over rights - Osborne challenges Chang’s stance on US deportation lawsuits, warns Jamaica could face scrutiny over rights safeguards.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 6 hours ago: Reckoning over rights - Osborne challenges Chang’s stance on US deportation lawsuits, warns Jamaica could face scrutiny over rights safeguards.
National Security Minister Dr Horace Chang’s assertion that legal challenges in the United States (US) against its third-country deportation policy are of no concern to Jamaica has drawn criticism from civil society advocate Kay Osborne. Osborne described Chang’s statement as a “convenient deflection”, arguing that it sidesteps the Government’s responsibility to protect human rights under international law, including the obligation not to transfer people to places where they face torture or persecution.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

- Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Russian drone strikes near school in Poltava Oblast, children were in shelter.
A Russian drone has struck near a school in Poltava Oblast. The blast wave damaged the school's windows. The children and staff were in a shelter at the time of the strike and were unharmed.
- The Moscow Times, 23 hours ago: Putin Convenes Top Russian Officials to Discuss Cybersecurity.
The Kremlin said the meeting was not connected with Ukrainian drone strikes in the past week on four Russian data centers.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Porcelain fish survives Russian strike on Kyiv apartment building and becomes symbol of resilience – photos.
An apartment belonging to volunteer and medic Andrii Dubenko in Kyiv's Lisovyi residential area was damaged during the Russian attack on the capital on 14 October.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Why Ukrainian strikes on data centers are a real problem for Russia — and beyond.
- Politico Europe, 9 hours ago: Why Ukrainian strikes on data centers are a real problem for Russia — and beyond.
Servers have become a target of war. As well as disrupting daily life, the strikes are raising questions of international law.
- Balkan Insight, 5 hours ago: Black Sea Drone Attacks Expose Holes in Bulgarian Security Strategy.
Military experts are alarmed at what they see as inaction on the part of Bulgaria’s government in the face of spillover from Russia’s war in Ukraine.
- Balkan Insight, 2 hours ago: Albanian PM Blames Opposition After Another Night of Violent Clashes.
Edi Rama accuses opposition of trying to 'pull Albania down' after a second night of violence saw government buildings and businesses attacked and set on fire amid clashes between student protesters and police.
- Politico Europe, 2 hours ago: Croatia pumps the brakes on Montenegro’s EU membership bid.
Zagreb is pressing Podgorica to resolve long-standing disputes over war crimes, compensation and border demarcation before wrapping up EU accession talks.

Russia's Pacific Fleet has test-fired cruise missiles from a nuclear-powered submarine, striking a target 1,200km away.
- Jerusalem Post, Al Jazeera - Middle East, just now: Could Israeli technology aid Saudi Arabia's struggles to stop Houthi missile attacks? - analysis.
Attacks on Riyadh’s airport and Saudi Aramco’s headquarters exposed gaps in the kingdom’s air defenses. Israeli technology and intelligence could help, but political barriers complicate cooperation.

[DW] Aid groups warn of an imminent collapse of the health system as fighting continues to displace civilians amid the planting season. The UN has extended an arms embargo, but only for Darfur.

Eritrean troops in Tigray have suffered "heavy losses" and are retreating towards their border, according to a spokesperson for an Ethiopian pro-government militia.
- Africanews, 20 hours ago: Nobel Peace Prize winner Navi Pillay hits out at US sanctions on ICC.
Just days after the 2026 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to Navi Pillay, the White House imposed fresh sanctions on the International Criminal Court. Pillay, the former UN human rights chief, says the timing was no coincidence.

[New Zimbabwe] THE Zambezi River Authority (ZRA) has slashed water allocations for power generation at Kariba Dam to 23 billion cubic metres (BCM) in 2027, warning of a potentially dry season due to El Niño conditions.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Elon Musk calls on Zelensky to 'go' as Ukraine leader.
- Dawn (Pakistan), NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: Elon Musk calls on Zelensky to 'go' as Ukraine leader.
Tech billionaire Elon Musk called on Wednesday for Volodymyr Zelensky to “go” as Ukraine’s president, as Kyiv raised doubts over US support for the war-torn country. Ukraine accused the United States this week of helping Russia by failing to warn it of incoming missile strikes and hobbling Kyiv’s military response through changes to Musk’s satellite system which it uses for communications. “And so the slaughter continues,” Musk wrote on X.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 8 hours ago: Two ships sink near Hormuz after being hit by projectiles.
LONDON: A container ship and a dry bulk carrier both sank near the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours after being hit by projectiles in separate incidents, maritime officials said on Wednesday. Attacks around the waterway have surged over the past 10 days, with Iran saying it is stepping up strikes in response to the US blockade of its ports and tougher sanctions introduced last month. The Singapore-flagged GFS Pride, a small container vessel with a capacity of 2,824 20-foot equivalent units (TEU), sank while sailing through the strait, according to maritime security sources.
- Dawn (Pakistan), Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: US considers hitting Iran with 'Mother of All Bombs': report.
The United States is considering using its biggest non-nuclear bomb against Iran if President Donald Trump should decide to renew combat in the war that has hit a deadlock, CNN reported on Thursday. The military is planning for the potential use of the GBU-43/B Massive Ordnance Air Blast (MOAB) bomb — better known by its nickname, the “Mother Of All Bombs” — to target Iranian energy infrastructure and nuclear sites, according to the news outlet, which quoted officials familiar with the matter.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 5 hours ago: IMF warns Gulf economies will not return to pre-war growth soon.
The International Monetary Fund expects energy-rich Middle Eastern economies to bounce back, but not in the medium term, the organisation’s regional chief said on Thursday, as fighting continued between Saudi Arabia and Yemen’s Houthis. The statement comes as the IMF projects a widespread contraction in Gulf economies following months of war that began in Iran and has now spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen, with maritime energy traffic still impacted.

Lorelai Jacinto had worked as a domestic helper in Riyadh for two and a half years before she flew home to the Philippines on September 19, increasingly worried that the conflict in the Middle East was making it unsafe to stay. “When the conflict with Iran happened, I started feeling like it wasn’t safe there any more because I was right there in Riyadh myself, so the bombing, the missiles, were closer to us,” Jacinto told This Week in Asia. “I got worried, I got scared that maybe I wouldn’t be...
- South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: Inside Nepal’s unending cycle of avalanches, floods and landslides.
Nepal has weathered three disasters in six weeks, including the deadly August flash flood, making this year one of the deadliest in a country where monsoon rains already frequently wreak havoc. Experts warn that climate change is only making matters worse. The rock-ice avalanche near the Nepal-Tibet border that opened the floodgates in the Bhotekoshi and Trishuli rivers on August 26 killed more than 1,450 people, with nearly 6,000 others still missing. It was followed by a massive landslide...
- South China Morning Post - China, 10 hours ago: Chinese scientists use open-source data to spot suspected Israeli electronic warfare units.
Chinese military scientists claim they have developed an algorithm that could help identify electronic warfare units using civil aviation flight data. The researchers said they had located two sources of interference that were spoofing their locations near Israel during the conflict with Iran. The team did not explain why they had focused on the Israeli military. The researchers estimated the locations of the two units as being near Haifa, with reported positioning errors between 10.9km and...
- South China Morning Post - China, 2 hours ago: Cross-border matchmaking can lead to financial ruin, Chinese police warn rural men.
Authorities in the central Chinese province of Hunan have warned of the potential risks of cross-border arranged marriages, saying some relationships lack genuine emotional foundations and can lead to financial ruin or legal trouble. Marriages can be risky when they are organised by illegal matchmaking agencies that charge high fees, according to a post on the Xintian county police branch’s social media account on Tuesday. For-profit international matchmaking is illegal in China. The post...
India - bottom line: Trouble beneath the waves: India’s submarine fleet is ageing and replacements are years away.
- Times of India - Top Stories, just now: Trouble beneath the waves: India’s submarine fleet is ageing and replacements are years away.
The Indian Navy is currently operating an ageing submarine fleet with plans for expansion by 2030. The current fleet consists of 16 conventional submarines and three strategic submarines. Significant delays have been experienced in the procurement of new vessels, including the planned P-75I program. The navy aims to enhance its capabilities with domestic and foreign collaborations for nuclear-powered attack submarines.
- Times of India - Top Stories, one hour ago: 'Why attack the batter?': Gavaskar fumes as Shamar Joseph hits Arshdeep Singh.
During the fourth T20I in Hyderabad, West Indies defeated India by 24 runs to level the series. Sunil Gavaskar expressed criticism towards Shamar Joseph after a bouncer hit Arshdeep Singh on the shoulder. Despite pain, Arshdeep chose to continue batting, which raised concerns over his injury. Gavaskar also highlighted the need for India's batters to take more responsibility during their chase.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Video: Royal Bengal Tiger Spotted Along Arunachal Road, 2-Wheelers Banned On 4-km Stretch.
The sighting comes amid heightened concern over tiger movement in the region, particularly after an earlier incident in which a police constable travelling on his motorcycle from Anini was reportedly killed in a tiger attack.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: Pakistan tests Fatah-II ballistic missile, same type intercepted during Operation Sindoor.
Pakistan's Army conducted a test launch of the Fatah-2 Extended Range hypersonic ballistic missile, enhancing its military capabilities. This missile provides improved precision and the ability to outmaneuver enemy defenses during engagements. The test is significant as it follows India's recent operations targeting threats within Pakistan's territory. The development of this missile is part of an evolving missile strategy amid regional military tensions.
